beats.beat: The company operates in two segments: infrastructure creation and operating a Ready Mix Concrete (RMC) plant.

Its infrastructure work covers railways (platforms, station buildings, gauge conversion, track laying), bridges (beam, cantilever, arch, suspension, cable‑stayed, truss), and roads (bituminous and concrete).

Contracts are won through a tender process: the client floats a tender, a pre‑bid meeting is held, the contractor bids, and the job is awarded to the lowest quote after a performance guarantee is deposited.

The company’s marquee clients include Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd, Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority, Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd., and several private entities.
Western Railway is the dominant customer, contributing 52% of the orders on hand and 57% of total revenue in Fiscal 2018.
The company’s operations are concentrated in Mumbai and Maharashtra, and it claims a healthy order book.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations declined from ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018, with intermittent fluctuations.
Net profit after adjustments was volatile: ₹0.96 crore (FY2014), ₹0.78 crore (FY2015), ₹0.33 crore (FY2016), ₹0.16 crore (FY2017), and a sharp increase to ₹3.15 crore in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) ranged from ₹6.76 crore (FY2017) to ₹9.46 crore (FY2015), with FY2018 at ₹9.29 crore.
Long‑term borrowings decreased from ₹5.87 crore (FY2014) to ₹1.33 crore (FY2018), while short‑term borrowings increased from ₹30.82 crore to ₹35.37 crore over the same period.
Key ratios: EPS of ₹1.31 (FY2016), ₹0.63 (FY2017), ₹12.59 (FY2018); RoNW of 4.14%, 1.97%, and 28.14% for the same years; NAV per share of ₹44.71 as of FY2018.
The company acknowledges negative cash flows in recent financial years, which could strain operations.

beats.beat: The sole promoter is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares, representing 90.949% of the pre‑issue capital.
Other directors (Bharat Kumar Parmar, Shree Prakash Singh, Mukesh Pandey) each hold 300 shares, while key management personnel include CFO Anchal Pachori (CA) and CS Mohit Soni (ACS).
No criminal cases have been filed against the directors, and none are on the RBI’s list of willful defaulters.
Related party transactions: loans taken from KMP/directors ₹68.4 lakhs in FY2018, director remuneration ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables to related parties ₹324.3 lakhs as of March 31, 2018.
Two companies promoted by the promoter—Al‑Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited—were struck off by the ROC in March 2016 due to non‑operation.
No independent appraisal or monitoring agency has been appointed for the IPO proceeds.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector contributes roughly 8% to India’s GDP (at constant prices) and is highly fragmented and working capital intensive.
Government flagship programmes such as the 100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, and Power for All are key demand drivers.
FDI norms have been eased in 15 sectors including real estate and construction development, providing further impetus.
The logistics sector in India was valued at US$160 billion in 2017 and is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% to US$215 billion by 2020.
India’s GDP growth was above 7% in 2017, and the index of eight core industries grew 4.2% in 2017‑18.
Headwinds include the slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches, and changes in government policies.
The industry is competitive with both organized and unorganized players.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is an infrastructure construction company focused on railway and road projects in Mumbai, with a ready‑mix concrete plant.
It is raising capital through a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares to fund working capital and general corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, and what it is raising.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 each at a price to be determined. There is no offer for sale.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited and the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
Net proceeds will be used to meet working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and for general corporate purposes (amount not disclosed).
The company has not appointed any independent agency to appraise the project, and no monitoring agency has been appointed; fund deployment will be monitored by the Audit Committee.

beats.beat: Customer concentration risk: 57% of revenue in Fiscal 2018 came from Indian Railways (primarily Western Railway). Losing this customer would cause a significant revenue dip.
Dependence on government contracts: revenue depends on winning tenders; any failure to secure new contracts would materially affect financial condition.
Negative cash flows in recent years could impair the company’s ability to meet obligations and fund operations.
Unsecured loans of ₹405.02 lakhs (as of March 31, 2018) are repayable on demand; any demand could strain liquidity.
Promoter‑related companies were struck off by ROC, and significant related‑party transactions exist, raising governance concerns.
